disease_label_per_paper: Piperacillin/tazobactam-induced drug fever in an elderly patient with HIV infection
presentation_summary: 63-year-old man with HIV infection, CKD stage 3, seizure disorder, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, and acute cholecystitis was treated nonoperatively with renal-adjusted piperacillin/tazobactam.

At initial emergency presentation he had vomiting, right upper quadrant pain, low-grade temperature 37.9 degC, heart rate 95/min, and CT/HIDA evidence of acute cholecystitis; this underlying admission diagnosis is preserved as context, not as the target drug fever leaf.
After starting piperacillin/tazobactam, WBC, neutrophils, bilirubin, and temperature normalized by day 2, but intermittent fever recurred on days 3-8, peaking at 39.4 degC.
During the fever recurrence he was clinically improving, tolerating diet, denied abdominal pain/tenderness, nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea, and pulse remained around 80-90/min during fever spikes.

Repeated CBC with differential, chest X-ray, urinalysis, lactic acid, and procalcitonin were within normal limits; six blood culture sets and three urine culture sets were negative; CT chest showed no active pulmonary disease.

There was no rash or eosinophilia. Fever normalized within 48 hours after piperacillin/tazobactam was stopped; this dechallenge evidence and the final adjudication are kept as confirmatory/non-ranking.

quality_warnings: Initial acute cholecystitis evidence is preserved as underlying context because the drug-fever snapshot is day 8 after clinical improvement.
Negative cultures, negative imaging workup, dechallenge, and final adjudication are non-ranking confirmatory evidence.
No DRESS, SJS/TEN, toxidrome, active sepsis, or drug-induced organ injury syndrome is encoded as the expected disease.
